items.title: The binary tree carries an HF-ordering whose smallest element is the root
items.author: Silvia Barbina; Enrique Casanovas
items.work: The elementary theory of free Steiner triple systems
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 820-821: the binary tree of height alpha admits an HF-ordering in which the root is the least element rather than the greatest. The proof (source lines 822-823) is two sentences: it takes the natural ordering, in which the root sits at the top, and reverses it. The substantive step is the assertion that the reversed order is still an HF-ordering, which the author states without a verification; what the card records is that the author's argument consists exactly of the reversal together with that assertion, and the statement records only the existence of the ordering with the root below everything.

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of the labelled lemma, retained line for line
